action: Teachers and staff: check the Office's notice for whether you are among the 158 affected; organisations: de-identify documents before sending them to outside parties.
date_note: Date of the Office's website notice as reported by DailySecu; the transfers it describes were on 6, 12, 15 and 18 May 2026.
exec: A public education body passed 158 teachers' personal data to outside parties in documents that were not de-identified, per its own notice.
geo_basis: organisation named in source; province capital (approx.)
impact: Per the Office's notice as reported by DailySecu: affiliation, name, date of birth, outside-employment permission, private-tuition company name, contract period, misconduct details and amounts received or paid.
plain: A South Korean provincial education office says personal details of 158 teachers were sent to outside parties without names being removed. It says the originals were destroyed.
summary: DailySecu reports that the Gyeonggi Provincial Office of Education disclosed, in a website notice dated 20 November, that personal information of 158 teachers was given to 5 case-related persons on 6, 12, 15 and 18 May 2026. Two documents submitted to the Teacher Appeals Review Commission had not been de-identified. The Office says it replaced them, confirmed the originals were destroyed and found no evidence of public disclosure.
title: Gyeonggi education office says 158 teachers' data went to outside parties in non-de-identified documents

validation.note: Only DailySecu read, which relays the Office's own 20 November notice; the notice itself was not read.

review.note: Compared title, summary, 158 teachers, 5 persons, May dates, two non-de-identified documents, data fields, replacement and destruction, no-disclosure statement and 20 Nov notice date against the DailySecu article
